title: What's new in iOS 26 and iOS 27
summary: iOS 26 introduced the Liquid Glass design and the on-device Foundation Models (LLM) framework. iOS 27 (WWDC26) makes Liquid Glass mandatory and expands the AI frameworks.
body: **iOS 26 (2025):** **Liquid Glass** - a new translucent design language across system UI (`glassEffect`, `GlassEffectContainer`, updated tab bars and toolbars). **Foundation Models framework** - use Apple's on-device language model from Swift: `LanguageModelSession`, structured output with `@Generable`/`@Guide`, streaming and tool calling, private and offline. Also: SwiftUI `WebView`, rich text editing with `AttributedString`, `@Animatable` macro, `BGContinuedProcessingTask`, Declared Age Range API.

**iOS 27 (WWDC26, as reported):** apps can no longer opt out of Liquid Glass (audit custom components); Foundation Models becomes provider-agnostic (Apple's models or cloud models through one protocol) with image input; Core AI for running custom models on device; an Evaluations framework to test AI features; SwiftUI list and layout performance improvements; agentic coding tools in Xcode 27. Confirm details against Apple's WWDC26 sessions.

**Staff angle:** talk about adoption plans, not lists. Example: the design-system team ships Liquid Glass-ready components and a checklist; an AI feature has a privacy review, a fallback when the model is not available, evaluation datasets and latency budgets.
keyPoints: iOS 26: Liquid Glass + on-device Foundation Models.
Guided generation (`@Generable`) gives typed, reliable model output.
Always check model availability and keep a non-AI fallback.
iOS 27: Liquid Glass mandatory; broader AI frameworks (verify specifics).
Frame answers as adoption strategy and risk management.

followups: **How do you ship an on-device LLM feature safely?** Check availability, feature-flag it, constrain output with guided generation, evaluate quality with test sets, keep a non-AI fallback, respect privacy.
